status_summary: No DOT or DOJ policy statement endorsing joint ventures among smaller carriers was found. On 2026-10-08 the FAA published an exemption letting JetBlue acquire 22 LaGuardia slots from Spirit, which had stopped flying on 2026-05-02 and was being liquidated, reasoning that the transfer helps a limited independent carrier compete with dominant carriers. DOJ was reported on 2026-03-16 to have cleared Allegiant's planned acquisition of Sun Country, two smaller carriers, with DOT approval still pending, and in April 2026 the Transportation Secretary was reported as open to airline mergers without committing to any. These are case-by-case steps in the direction of the text, not the public posture it asks for.

timeline.event: DOJ was reported to have cleared Allegiant's planned acquisition of Sun Country, two smaller carriers, with DOT approval still required (news report, date from article timestamp).

FAA granted a joint JetBlue and Spirit petition for an exemption allowing 22 LaGuardia slots to move from Spirit, which had ceased operations on 2026-05-02 and was in liquidation, to JetBlue; the order says the transfer helps a limited independent low-fare carrier compete with dominant carriers and bars trading or leasing the slots before April 2028.

title: Signal support for joint ventures by smaller airlines such as JetBlue and Spirit
uncertainties: The 2025-07-29 completion of DOT's review of the JetBlue and United Blue Sky partnership was announced by the companies, involves United, one of the four large carriers, and does not match the smaller-carrier joint venture the text describes, so it is kept as a source and not as an event. The Spirit slot transfer followed a bankruptcy auction and is an asset sale, not a joint venture. The Allegiant and Sun Country clearance and the April 2026 remarks of the Secretary rest on trade press; a DOJ or DOT primary release was not opened, and whether DOT approved the Allegiant and Sun Country combination was not checked. Searches on DOT and DOJ airline consolidation policy statements found no formal policy document.
